quizzes.stem: A finance analyst wants Claude to turn a folder of invoices into a reconciled spreadsheet and a summary, handled on its own while they are in meetings. Which choice fits?

options.a: Add the invoices to a Project, then request the sheet and summary in chat
options.b: Upload the invoices to a chat and ask for both outputs in a single turn
options.c: Attach the whole company drive so that nothing the task needs is missing
options.d: Delegate it to Cowork with a dedicated directory, then inspect the result

explanation.d: There is a clear deliverable that touches files, so it is a delegation, and a dedicated folder keeps the reach narrow (the worked task).
explanation.b: Ruled out because chat is best for "work light on files and sources", and a folder of invoices is heavy on files.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the safety habits say to "create a dedicated working folder" and not to grant whole drives.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a Project still works as chat, "A conversation you steer turn by turn", while "A clear deliverable that touches your files or tools" that runs on its own during meetings is what Cowork is for.

quizzes.stem: A team lead sets up a weekly Cowork task that reads a shared inbox and replies to customers. On the first scheduled run no one is watching. What should the team lead change first?

options.a: Limit early runs to summarising messages, so someone reviews each output
options.b: Start in Auto mode, as it checks every action for safety on its own
options.c: Connect the folder of past replies too, so drafts can match earlier answers
options.d: Run it daily rather than weekly, so that any mistakes surface sooner

explanation.a: Replying to customers is a consequential action, and the page says to start scheduled tasks with low-risk work such as summaries and to review the output after each run.
explanation.b: Ruled out because Auto mode checks each action "but it still runs on its own", and the habits recommend Manual approval for new tools and hard-to-undo actions.
explanation.c: Ruled out because more context leaves the cause in place: "Scheduled tasks run while you are away, so you cannot watch them", and the replies would still go out unchecked.
explanation.d: Ruled out because more frequent runs only repeat errors faster: "A recurring task repeats its mistakes unattended".

quizzes.stem: A user connects a documents folder and their mailbox to Cowork. One file carries an invisible instruction telling Claude to mail the folder's contents to an address. The user relies on the cloud environment for protection. Why can this still cause harm?

options.a: The hidden text can reach the home network from inside the sandbox
options.b: The hidden text stays in the sandbox and acts again in later sessions
options.c: The hidden text can send messages via a linked tool the sandbox leaves open
options.d: The hidden text lets Claude reach folders the user never connected

explanation.c: The isolation "doesn't limit what Claude reads or does" through the connected tools, so the protection covers the network and not what Claude can send through the connected mailbox.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the environment "is removed when the session ends", so nothing in it carries into a later session.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the sandbox "cannot reach your home or company network", which is the part isolation does protect.
explanation.d: Ruled out because Claude "reaches only folders you explicitly connected", and the harm here comes from what it already reaches.

quizzes.stem: An operations lead runs Claude in Chrome in Automatically approve mode on a supplier portal. A page there holds white-on-white text telling the assistant to settle an open invoice through the portal's payment form. What happens?

options.a: Claude follows the text, since the portal is a site the lead chose to visit
options.b: The extension strips hidden text before reading, so it never reaches Claude
options.c: Claude asks the lead for approval at the form, then settles it once they agree
options.d: Screening covers each step, and transactions are off limits under any setting

explanation.d:
The page describes classifiers that screen incoming content and each action, and "Making purchases or
   financial transactions" is prohibited regardless of permission mode, so the invoice is not settled.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because the page lists "completing
   instructions found in emails or web content" among the actions that are off limits.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because the
   page's own risk is "invisible text that tells Claude to fetch bank statements", which "Claude's classifiers screen
   incoming content" to catch, so such text does reach Claude.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because the permissions guide lists
   "Making purchases or financial transactions" among the actions Claude is prohibited from "regardless of permission
   mode", so no approval from the lead lets the payment go through.

quizzes.stem: An Enterprise team has the Compliance API enabled, and wants that API to hold a record of the Excel add-in's use, governed by the organisation's custom rules on how long data is kept. Which gap should the team expect?

options.a: Sessions are captured there, but the in-house retention policy does not cover them
options.b: The audit logs record the sessions, but the Compliance API leaves them out
options.c: Chat history sits on Anthropic's servers, beyond the in-house retention policy
options.d: Sessions are captured there, but the backend keeps them until an admin deletes them

explanation.a:
The page says add-in sessions are included in the Compliance API, but the add-ins "do not inherit
   your organisation's custom data-retention settings", so the record exists and the team's own rules do not govern
   it.
explanation.d:
Ruled out because "Inputs and outputs are deleted from Anthropic's backend within 30 days", with no
   admin step.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because "their activity is not in the Enterprise audit logs", while "add-in sessions
   are included in it" for Enterprise organisations with the Compliance API enabled.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "Chat
   history is stored in your browser, not on Anthropic's servers".

quizzes.stem: A manager wants Claude Tag to draft a delicate reply from their saved connectors, hidden from the team, with the usage counted against their individual account. Where should they write to it?

options.a: In a channel where an admin set up the connectors for everyone there
options.b: In a direct message of their own, outside any channel
options.c: In a channel, then ask Claude to hide the reply afterwards
options.d: In a group direct message with one trusted colleague

explanation.b:
A direct message uses "Your own claude.ai account and your own connectors", and only you see it (the
   table).
explanation.a:
Ruled out because a channel gives "What an admin set up for that channel; everyone there gets the
   same access" and the organisation pays.
explanation.d:
Ruled out because a group direct message uses "The access an admin
   set for the workspace" and is paid by the organisation.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "Work in a channel is visible to
   everyone there and uses the channel's access", so hiding the reply later does not undo that.

quizzes.stem: A recruiter needs one short, polite decline email for a single candidate, with the facts supplied. Which surface suits it best?

options.a: Plain chat, with a quick check of the details before sending
options.b: Cowork on a dedicated folder holding the candidate's file
options.c: A shared Project holding every past letter, opened to the team
options.d: A Research run that gathers sources on rejection etiquette

explanation.a: A single short draft needs none of the machinery; plain chat plus a check of the facts is enough (task 6).
explanation.b: Ruled out because for a single draft "adding a Project or Cowork would add setup, allowance use and risk with no gain".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A shared Project, a published artifact and a shared skill show their content to everyone with access", which is a poor home for candidate details.
explanation.d: Ruled out because Research is for an open question with many sources, and the table lists "A job one document answers" as what Research must not be given.

quizzes.stem: A product team wants one visible place in Slack to chase open checklist entries, where anyone can steer the work. One entry is a pay dispute. Which approach fits?

options.a: Keep routine items in the thread, and flag the HR matter there as sensitive
options.b: Keep routine items in the thread, and move the HR matter to a shared Project
options.c: Move every item to a direct message, and post the results to the thread
options.d: Keep routine items in the thread, and keep the HR matter out of the tool

explanation.d:
A channel suits shared work that anyone can steer (task 5), while a sensitive HR matter belongs
   with the people and policy that govern it, so the pay dispute stays out of the tool.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because a sensitive HR matter belongs "not in a tool
   whose results the whole channel can read", and a sensitivity mark does not hide it.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because the table says chat surfaces must not be given
   "a shared Project holding material the audience may not see", and the team would see the dispute.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because the channel is chosen "so the
   thread is visible and anyone can steer it", and work done in a direct message leaves nobody else able to steer.

quizzes.stem: An analyst is editing a pricing workbook in Excel, and has the sales deck and cover memo built on its figures open beside it in PowerPoint and Word. A discount rate changes, and the new numbers must reach all three. Which surface fits best?

options.a: Claude Tag in a channel, with the three files attached
options.b: A Project whose knowledge base holds the workbook, deck and memo
options.c: The Microsoft 365 add-ins, set to let Claude act across files
options.d: Cowork on a connected folder holding copies of the three files

explanation.c: The work lives in open Excel, PowerPoint and Word files and context passes between them (task 3).
explanation.b: Ruled out because a Project suits "Recurring work with fixed rules and reference files", and does not edit the open files.
explanation.a: Ruled out because Claude Tag reaches "The thread, what an admin connected, public channels by search", while the figures must change in "The files and mail open at that moment".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the checklist gives Cowork "A multi-step job over files and tools" and gives "A task inside an open Office file" to the add-in, and these files are open in their apps, so copies in a folder would leave them as they were.

quizzes.stem: A team sets up a Cowork job that reads supplier meeting notes and updates the rows of a shared action tracker. They want it in Auto approval, running weekly from the first week, and checking last year's notes kept elsewhere on the drive. Which plan does the module support?

options.a: Approve actions by hand, open the drive wide to the job, then run it every week
options.b: Move it to the Excel add-in, let it reach notes on the drive, then run it weekly
options.c: Approve actions by hand, use one dedicated folder, then schedule after clean runs
options.d: Leave Auto approval on, give it one folder for both years, then schedule once runs are clean

explanation.c:
The habits say to use Manual approval for new tools and hard-to-undo actions, to grant access selectively,
   and to start scheduled tasks simple and review each run (Cowork page).
explanation.a:
Ruled out because the habits say to
   "grant access selectively and avoid financial documents, credentials and personal records", and an entire drive
   does the opposite.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because the add-in can "read and write only files that are open at that
   moment".
explanation.d:
Ruled out because the first runs use Manual "because the task is new and writes files", and
   updating the tracker's rows writes files from the very first run.

quizzes.stem: A consultant opens a spreadsheet from an unknown sender in Excel with the add-in, and asks Claude to update the assumptions. The cells hide text telling Claude to send data elsewhere. Which handling fits?

options.a: Ask Claude in Chrome to open the sender's page and compare the figures
options.b: Turn on cross-app work, so that a second document checks each change
options.c: Make the edits manually, and keep the assistant off this workbook
options.d: Rely on Auto approval, which blocks anything unsafe in Office files

explanation.c: The add-in page says to "only use it with trusted spreadsheets", and a workbook from an unknown sender with hidden instructions is not one.
explanation.b: Ruled out because with cross-app work "one conversation can read an Excel model and write a Word memo or a slide", which widens what the hidden text can reach.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the Chrome habits say to "avoid unfamiliar pages or those with content from unknown people", and the sender's page is one.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the Auto mode described is for Chrome and Cowork, and the add-in page warns that "files from outside sources can contain hidden instructions".

quizzes.stem: Contractors from a partner firm are added to a project channel where Claude Tag files and updates tickets for staff in the company's ticket tool. The contractors must not be able to file or change tickets through Claude. What should the organisation do?

options.a: Have an admin choose which members are allowed to call on the assistant
options.b: Disconnect the workspace from Claude until the contractors have left
options.c: Have the staff use Claude only through their own direct messages
options.d: Give Claude's ticket account the narrowest role that covers the work

explanation.a:
In a channel everyone gets the same access, and "Admins can restrict who can invoke Claude and where it
   works", which is the check a channel that gained guests deserves (pages 2 and 3).
explanation.d:
Ruled out because "the
   narrowest role that covers the work" still lets Claude file and change tickets, and in a channel "everyone there gets the same
   access", so the contractors could use it too.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because disconnecting a workspace "permanently
   deletes that workspace's Claude data", far more than the change needs.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because a direct message
   changes only the staff's route to "Your own claude.ai account and your own connectors", and the channel set-up
   stays open to the contractors.

quizzes.stem: Each month a facilities manager wants help to go through contractors' repair write-ups stored as files, update a spreadsheet of overdue jobs, and share the list where all their colleagues can see it and steer the follow-ups. Which combination fits best?

options.a: Plain chat with the write-ups uploaded, then Claude Tag in the team channel
options.b: Cowork on a dedicated reports folder, then Claude Tag in the team channel
options.c: Cowork on one folder of the write-ups, then Claude Tag in a direct message
options.d: The Excel add-in on the open spreadsheet, then Claude Tag in the team channel

explanation.b: A multi-step job over files is Cowork, kept to a dedicated folder, and work the whole team must see and steer belongs in a channel (pages 1 and 3).
explanation.a: Ruled out because chat is best for "work light on files and sources", and a month of write-ups plus a spreadsheet to update is a multi-step job over files.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Claude Tag in a channel shows everything to everyone in the channel; a direct message does not", so the colleagues could neither see the list nor steer the follow-ups.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Claude can read and write only files that are open at that moment" and "it cannot open, create or switch files itself", so the add-in cannot work through the stored write-ups.
